metadata.title: CrowdStrike buying Zscaler as cybersecurity consolidates

content.text:
CrowdStrike on Monday said it's agreed to acquire cybersecurity firm Zscaler for around $43.9 billion in stock.
Why it matters: Cyber consolidation is accelerating as companies seek to defend against both AI-enabled threats and AI-discovered security holes.
By the numbers: Zscaler shareholders will receive an implied value of $260.41 per share, which represents a 34% premium to Friday's closing price.
Go deeper, via Bloomberg: "The deal will pitch CrowdStrike into greater competition with Palo Alto Networks and Microsoft and underscores the shift toward a smaller number of companies protecting more of the world's computers and networks."
